created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the assistant was created.

description.description: The description of the assistant. The maximum length is 512 characters.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

instructions.description: The system instructions that the assistant uses. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

metadata.description: Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Keys can be a maximum of 64 characters long and values can be a maxium of 512 characters long.

model.description: ID of the model to use. You can use the List models API to see all of your available models.

name.description: The name of the assistant. The maximum length is 256 characters.

object.description: The object type, which is always assistant.

description.description: A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to determine how to respond in the format.

name.description: The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object.

schema.description: The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.

strict.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output. If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined in the schema field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when strict is true.

json_schema.description: Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with GPT-4o, GPT-4 Turbo, and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since gpt-3.5-turbo-1106.

type.description: Setting to {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} } enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Setting to { "type": "json_object" } enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.

response_format.description: Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with GPT-4o, GPT-4 Turbo, and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since gpt-3.5-turbo-1106.

temperature.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.

file_ids.description: A list of file IDs attached to this assistant. There can be a maximum of 20 files attached to the assistant. Files are ordered by their creation date in ascending order.

code_interpreter.description: Function definition for tools of type function.

vector_store_ids.description: A list of file IDs attached to this assistant. There can be a maximum of 20 files attached to the assistant. Files are ordered by their creation date in ascending order.

file_search.description: Function definition for tools of type function.

tool_resources.description: A set of resources that are used by the assistant's tools. The resources are specific to the type of tool. For example, the code_interpreter tool requires a list of file IDs, while the file_search tool requires a list of vector store IDs.

description.description: A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

name.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

parameters.description: The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object.

function.description: Function definition for tools of type function.

type.description: Tools can be of types code_interpreter, retrieval, or function.

tools.description: A list of tool enabled on the assistant. There can be a maximum of 128 tools per assistant. Tools can be of types code_interpreter, retrieval, or function.

top_p.description: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

project_id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

block.description: Represents an individual project service account.

anchor.description: Anchor timestamp after which the expiration policy applies.

days.description: The number of days after the anchor time that the vector store will expire.

expires_after.description: The expiration policy for a vector store.

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the vector store will expire.

cancelled.description: The number of files that were cancelled.

completed.description: The number of files that have been successfully processed.

failed.description: The number of files that have failed to process.

in_progress.description: The number of files that are currently being processed.

file_counts.description: The expiration policy for a vector store.

file_ids.description: A list of file IDs attached to this vector store. There can be a maximum of 20 files attached to the assistant. Files are ordered by their creation date in ascending order.

last_active_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the vector store was last active.

metadata.description: Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to a vector store. This can be useful for storing additional information about the vector store in a structured format. Keys can be a maximum of 64 characters long and values can be a maxium of 512 characters long.

object.description: The object type, which is always vector_store.

status.description: The status of the vector store, which can be either expired, in_progress, or completed. A status of completed indicates that the vector store is ready for use.

usage_bytes.description: The total number of bytes used by the files in the vector store.
